title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.

providers.name: Slack
providers.scope_notes: SAML SSO is available on Business+ and Enterprise, and on Free/Pro only with a connected Salesforce org. EMA uses organization-level installations and MCP user tokens.

controls.name: Require approved apps (Only allow pre-approved apps)
controls.what: Members can only install pre-approved apps; others must be requested and approved, and approval covers the scopes the app will use.
controls.setting: Admin > Apps and workflows > App Management Settings > Require approved apps
controls.quote: Apps connect third-party services to Slack, and by default, members can install them without approval from a Workspace Owner. If they'd like, Workspace Owners can enable app approval to pre-approve or restrict certain apps for their workspace.

controls.name: Restrict app
controls.what: Blocks members from installing or requesting a specific app; existing installs keep working until uninstalled.
controls.setting: Admin > Apps and workflows > Browse > [app] > Restrict
controls.quote: If an app you restrict has already been installed to your workspace, members can continue using it. You can uninstall any app you don't want people to use.

controls.name: App Management policy (Require App Approval)
controls.what: Turns on app approval for every workspace in the Enterprise org.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > App Management > Add Policy
controls.quote: Setting an app management policy turns on app approval for every workspace in an org. When app approval is enabled, members can only use apps that have been approved for their workspaces.

controls.name: Restrict for Organization
controls.what: Org Owners/Admins can block an app from being installed anywhere in the org when reviewing a request.
controls.setting: Org app request notification > Restrict for Organization; or admin.apps.restrict API
controls.quote: Select Approve for Organization or Restrict for Organization . Choosing Restrict for Organization will prevent all members from installing the app.

controls.name: Token rotation policy
controls.what: Requires OAuth token rotation for apps and expires unused refresh tokens after 30 days; applies only to installs and updates after it is turned on.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > Token rotation > Add Policy
controls.quote: Token rotation Require OAuth token rotation for apps and automatically expire unused refresh tokens after 30 days. Note: Changing these settings doesn't affect existing apps.

controls.name: Slack Marketplace installations policy
controls.what: Limits members to installing apps listed in the Slack Marketplace.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > Slack Marketplace installations
controls.quote: Slack Marketplace installations Only allow members to install apps from the Slack Marketplace .

controls.name: Member Permissions: who can use the app
controls.what: Limits which members (everyone, no one, or specific people/groups) can initiate interaction with an installed app.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps > [app] > Member Permissions > Who has permission to initiate interaction with this app
controls.quote: Choose who can use the app — Everyone , No one , or Specific people and groups .

controls.name: Member Permissions: where can this app be used
controls.what: Limits an installed app to all channels, only specific channels, or all channels except some.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps > [app] > Member Permissions > Where can this app be used
controls.quote: Next to Where can this app be used , click Edit . Choose where the app can appear — All channels , Only specific channels , or All channels except...

controls.name: Remove or uninstall an org-level app
controls.what: Org admins can remove an org-installed app from workspaces or uninstall it from the whole org.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps; or admin.apps.uninstall API
controls.quote: There are two options for removing apps installed at the org level: Remove the app from workspaces that no longer need to use it. Uninstall the app from your org to remove it from all workspaces.

controls.name: Restrict API Token Usage (Allowed IP Address Ranges)
controls.what: Rejects Web API, SCIM API and MCP server calls made with the app's tokens from IPs not on the list (max 20 IPv4 entries).
controls.setting: App settings > OAuth & Permissions > Restrict API Token Usage

controls_unknown: No tenant-admin IP allowlist for app tokens found; 'Restrict API Token Usage' IP ranges are set by the app developer in app config, not by workspace admins.
Whether admins can force-revoke individual user tokens without uninstalling the app.
Whether EMA lets admins restrict MCP scopes beyond IdP assignment.

authentication.summary: OAuth bot/user bearer tokens; app-level tokens for selected functions.

federation.details: Enterprise-managed authorization exchanges external IdP ID-JAGs for user access to Slack MCP. It is not general bot/workload federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: App-level allowlist supports up to 20 IPv4 ranges for Web API and SCIM. Incoming webhooks are excluded.

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens are single-use; keep the newly returned refresh token. They do not expire on a schedule by default, but for PKCE-enabled apps all refresh tokens expire after 30 days.

administration.summary: Bot/user scopes, app approval/install controls, token revocation and rotation; EMA permissions delegated through IdP configuration.
administration.conditions: SAML SSO requires eligible Business+/Enterprise tiers. EMA uses organization-level installations and MCP user tokens.

offboard.details: User tokens are revoked when the authorizing member is deactivated; bot tokens are tied to the app and keep working.

inventory.details: Org admins can list installed apps (Integrations > Installed apps, Export CSV), not individual tokens.

reads.ui: Organization settings > Security > Audit logs > Filter > Events (file downloaded) and Acting user

kill.ui: Tools & settings > Manage apps > Installed Apps > App Details > Configuration > Remove App
kill.api: GET https://slack.com/api/auth.revoke (immediate, single token); POST https://slack.com/api/apps.uninstall or admin.apps.uninstall (revokes all installation tokens incl. refresh)

offboard.ui: Enterprise: Organization settings > People > Members > select > Deactivate. Other plans: Admin > Workspace settings > People > three dots > Deactivate account

token_format.notes: Access tokens expire after 43,200 s (12 h). Refresh tokens are single-use. Rotation cannot be turned off once enabled. Regex is a loose prefix match.

log_sources.name: Slack Audit Logs API (GET https://api.slack.com/audit/v1/logs)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise plan. Same app lifecycle events as non-rotating tokens; no documented event for individual token refresh.

credential_id_fields.notes: User behind a rotating user token

lifecycle_events.notes: First access + refresh token pair issued

anomaly_cues: Leaked refresh token (xoxe-1-) is worse than a leaked access token: it mints new 12 h tokens until revoked or app uninstalled
Legitimate app suddenly fails to refresh (attacker redeemed the single-use refresh token first)
anomaly ip_address with new-asn or cloud-asn for an app that normally runs from fixed egress
Access token seen in use far beyond 12 h after its leak time indicates refresh token or client secret also leaked

containment.steps: auth.revoke the access token(s); uninstall the app (apps.uninstall / admin.apps.uninstall) to kill the refresh chain; rotate client_secret since it is required for refresh; reinstall.
containment.notes: Refreshing does not immediately invalidate the old access token; old refresh token is revoked after a short grace period. auth.revoke revokes a single token without changing the installation. Up to 2 active access tokens can exist at once.

sample_query.language: Slack Audit Logs API (GET /audit/v1/logs query parameters)
sample_query.purpose: Pull anomaly events, then filter entity.type=app and details.reason ip_address/tor/unexpected_credential_testing

calls.reveals: New 12-hour xoxe. access token plus a new refresh token
calls.log_notes: No Slack audit action documented for refreshing an app's own rotating token.

calls.reveals: team, user, team_id, user_id, url (bot_id for bot tokens)
calls.log_notes: No documented audit action for auth.test; the app-only anomaly unexpected_credential_testing may fire on suspicious validity testing (Enterprise only).

calls.reveals: Channels and DMs the token can see
calls.log_notes: No documented audit action for this read.

calls.reveals: Full message history of a channel
calls.rate_limit: Tier 3: 50+/min; 1/min and 15 objects for new non-Marketplace commercial apps (since 2025-05-29)
calls.log_notes: No documented audit action for API message reads; audit logs do not expose message content.
Enterprise audit action 'A file was downloaded or viewed within Slack'; docs do not state whether API-driven downloads emit it. Anomaly excessive_downloads covers apps and users.
